findings.title: i18next placeholder syntax broken for error-invalid-multivalued-size
findings.body: The value for error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from the i18next double-curly-brace interpolation format (`Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).`) to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`, which uses single curly braces plus Java's MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax. Every other key in this file (backTo=Back to {{app}}, setUpNew=Set up {{name}}, credentialCreatedAt=<0>Created</0> {{date}}., etc.) uses the `{{var}}` convention required by i18next in the React Account Console. Because i18next does not interpret `{0}` or `{2,choice,...}` syntax, this key will no longer be interpolated at all: end users will literally see `{0}`, `{1}`, `{2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}` in the error message instead of the real attribute name/limits. This looks like the Java-side ChoiceFormat fix needed to satisfy the new HTML sanitizer in the Java theme bundles was mistakenly copy-pasted into this unrelated JS/i18next resource file.

findings.title: Same i18next placeholder regression in Admin Console messages
findings.body: error-invalid-multivalued-size was changed from `Attribute {{0}} must have at least {{1}} and at most {{2}} value(s).` to `Attribute {0} must have at least {1} and at most {2} {2,choice,0#values|1#value|1<values}.`. As with the Account Console file, this admin-ui properties file is consumed by i18next which requires `{{var}}` double-brace interpolation, not single braces or Java MessageFormat ChoiceFormat syntax. This will show the raw placeholder text to Admin Console users instead of a properly formatted validation error, and is inconsistent with every other key in the surrounding file that still uses double braces.

findings.title: Lithuanian translation replaced with Italian text
findings.body: The fix for totpStep1 (removing a mismatched anchor href flagged by the new HTML sanitizer) replaced the Lithuanian sentence with Italian text: 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:' (Italian for 'Install one of the following applications on your phone'). This is not Lithuanian, so Lithuanian-speaking Account Console users configuring OTP will now see Italian instructions. Compare with the correctly localized equivalent fixes done in the same PR for Finnish ('Asenna jokin seuraavista sovelluksista matkapuhelimeesi:'), Slovak ('Nainštalujte si do mobilu jednu z nasledujúcich aplikácií:') and Swedish ('Installera en av följande applikationer på din mobil:').

findings.title: Lithuanian login translation also replaced with Italian text
findings.body: loginTotpStep1 was changed to 'Installa una delle seguenti applicazioni sul tuo cellulare:', which is Italian, not Lithuanian. The same erroneous text was introduced here and in the account messages_lt.properties file (totpStep1), so Lithuanian users will see Italian setup instructions on both the login flow and the account console when configuring a mobile authenticator.

findings.title: Simplified Chinese (zh_CN) totpStep1 replaced with Traditional Chinese text
findings.body: The new value for totpStep1, '在您的手機上安裝以下應用程式之一：', uses Traditional Chinese characters (手機, 安裝, 應用程式), but this file's locale is zh_CN (Simplified Chinese). Every other string in the same file uses Simplified characters (e.g. mobile=手机, totpStep2=打开应用扫描二维码输入验证码, totpStep3=输入应用提供的一次性验证码单击保存). Mixing Traditional characters into a Simplified-Chinese locale file is a localization regression for mainland-China users and suggests the fix for this key accidentally reused the zh_TW translation instead of a Simplified-Chinese one.

findings.title: Property files are read as ISO-8859-1 instead of UTF-8
findings.body: verifySafeHtml() loads both the checked file and the English reference file via `new PropertyResourceBundle(new FileInputStream(...))`. PropertyResourceBundle's InputStream constructor always decodes the stream as ISO-8859-1, but the actual .properties files in this repository contain literal UTF-8 multi-byte characters (Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai, Korean, CJK, etc., as seen throughout this diff) rather than \uXXXX escapes. Reading them with the wrong charset corrupts every non-ASCII character into mojibake. ASCII-only HTML tags are unaffected, but the diagnostic text appended via messages.add(...) (e.g. 'Illegal HTML in key ... for file ...: ...') will show garbled fragments of the surrounding translated sentence, undermining the usefulness of the new sanitizer's error output for the very (non-English) locale files it is meant to help fix.

findings.title: Brittle derivation of the English reference file path can crash the build ungracefully
findings.body: The English reference bundle path is derived purely by string substitution on the absolute path of the checked file (replaceAll("resources-community", "resources") then replacing the locale suffix with "_en.properties"). This assumes every checked file lives under a path containing the literal substring 'resources-community' and is named '..._<locale>.properties'. Any theme/module with a different layout, or any file without that exact suffix pattern, will make `new FileInputStream(englishFile)` throw FileNotFoundException, which is caught and rethrown as an unchecked RuntimeException (line 79). Since verify() (lines 46-56) only catches the checked IOException and wraps it in MojoExecutionException, this RuntimeException propagates out of the Mojo uncaught, producing a raw stack trace instead of the structured Mojo failure used for the other checks in this class.

findings.title: Anchor mismatch leaves partially-stripped HTML, causing duplicate error messages
findings.body: santizeAnchors stops removing matched / tags as soon as it hits a mismatch and breaks out of the loop (line 158), leaving the mismatched tag (and any after it) still embedded in the returned value. verifySafeHtml() subsequently runs the HTML policy sanitizer over that same value, so the still-embedded anchor tag is flagged again as 'Illegal HTML'. A single changed/malicious link therefore produces two separate messages ('Didn't find anchor tag ...' and 'Illegal HTML in key ...') for the same root cause, which can be confusing when triaging a CI failure.

findings.title: Check is sensitive to the sanitizer's own serialization, not just real HTML safety
findings.body:
The sanitized output of policy.sanitize(value) is compared byte-for-byte to the original value. The OWASP sanitizer re-serializes self-closing elements with a space before '/>' (turning '
' into '
'), so a translation using the equally valid '
' form fails the check even though there is no actual markup injection. This PR had to edit dozens of locale files (ar, ca, cs, de, el, es, fa, fi, hr, ka, ko, sk, th, tr, uk, zh_CN, zh_TW, fr, en, etc.) purely to insert a space before '/>' to satisfy the sanitizer's canonical form. Future translation contributions using '
' will fail CI with a misleading 'Illegal HTML' message unrelated to security.

findings.title: Test fixture contains malformed HTML (missing closing bracket)
findings.body:
The fixture value is `key=Some
tag' and the file has no trailing newline. This appears to be an unintentional typo (likely meant to be `
`); the test still happens to fail because of the unmatched `
` opening tag, but the fixture does not actually represent a well-formed-but-disallowed HTML tag as its name implies, reducing confidence that the scenario is tested as intended.

findings.title: No regression test for HTML that legitimately matches between English and translation
findings.body:
All four tests in this file check failure scenarios (disallowed tag, HTML added only in the translation, mismatched anchor href). There is no fixture/test asserting that a translation whose HTML matches the English source exactly (e.g. both containing an identical `...`) passes with zero messages. Given how sensitive the comparison is to exact formatting (the PR had to rewrite `
` to `
` across dozens of locale files to satisfy it), a positive test would help guard against future regressions where legitimately matching, safe HTML starts being flagged as illegal.
